title: OpenAI's ad business hits $1B annualized revenue run rate
content:
OpenAI on Monday announced that its advertising business has hit $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate, a milestone that the company is touting as proof of its "diversified business model."
The artificial intelligence company is gearing up for what is expected to be a massive IPO, and is under pressure to justify its $852 billion valuation to investors. OpenAI said Monday that its ad business, which is roughly 200 days old, builds on its existing revenue engines like its enterprise offerings, consumer subscriptions and usage-based application programming interfaces.
OpenAI began testing ads within its ChatGPT chatbot in the U.S. in February, a decision that was both highly anticipated and controversial. Digital advertising has long been the cash cow for other big tech companies like Google and Meta, but OpenAI's move was ridiculed by its chief rival, Anthropic, which made OpenAI's ad push the focus of its first Super Bowl campaign.
ChatGPT Ads are now available in more than 40 countries, and OpenAI said it's rolling out self-service access across India, Europe, the Middle East and North Africa on Monday. Ads within the chatbot appear for OpenAI's Go subscribers and its free tier, which makes up the vast majority of its 1 billion weekly active users.
OpenAI said Monday that its ads are clearly labeled and do not influence ChatGPT's answers. Advertisers do not have access to users' private conversations.
"Our next phase of growth will bring ChatGPT Ads to more markets and introduce additional formats, objectives, buying options, and measurement capabilities," OpenAI said in a release. "We will also explore new ways for businesses to interact with consumers in more native ways in ChatGPT."
—CNBC's Kate Rooney contributed to this report

report.summary: OpenAI's advertising business reached $1 billion annualized revenue run rate, boosting its case for a massive IPO.
report.background: OpenAI is preparing for a highly anticipated IPO and needs to justify its $852 billion valuation to investors. Advertising has long been the core revenue engine for tech giants like Google and Meta, but OpenAI’s pivot into ads marks a major strategic shift for an AI company that previously relied on subscriptions, enterprise contracts, and API usage. The company began testing ChatGPT ads in the U.S. in February, a controversial move that Anthropic mocked during the Super Bowl. Now, roughly 200 days later, the ad business has hit a $1 billion annualized run rate, with ads live in more than 40 countries and self-service access expanding across India, Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa. The fast growth signals that consumer AI can support a diversified monetization model, but it also raises questions about user trust, data privacy, and the long-term impact on ChatGPT’s user experience.
key_points: OpenAI’s ad business reached a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate in about 200 days, a key milestone ahead of its expected IPO. The company is using this growth to show investors that it has multiple revenue streams beyond subscriptions and API sales.

ChatGPT ads are now available in over 40 countries and are expanding to more regions with self-service access. Ads appear for free tier users and Go subscribers, meaning the vast majority of OpenAI’s 1 billion weekly active users may see them.

OpenAI stresses that ads are clearly labeled and do not affect ChatGPT’s answers. Advertisers cannot access private conversations, an attempt to address privacy concerns that have followed the rollout.

The ad push is controversial and has been publicly ridiculed by rival Anthropic, which made fun of OpenAI’s ad strategy in a Super Bowl campaign. This highlights the competitive tension between the two AI firms as both consider going public.

The milestone helps OpenAI diversify its business model, which is critical for an $852 billion valuation. However, it also means users may face more advertising as OpenAI balances monetization with trust and experience.
report.impact: This development signals that advertising is becoming a viable revenue model for consumer AI, potentially reshaping how AI chatbots are funded. For the AI industry, it sets a precedent that free AI services can be ad-supported, but it also intensifies pressure on rivals like Google, Meta, and Anthropic to clarify their monetization strategies. Developers and businesses may benefit from new self-serve ad tools and APIs to reach ChatGPT’s massive audience. Regular users, especially those on the free tier, will likely see more ads and must trust that their conversations remain private. The biggest risk is that ads erode user trust or degrade the perceived neutrality of AI answers, which could hurt OpenAI’s reputation and IPO prospects. Ultimately, the company must prove that ad growth can continue without damaging the product experience.
report.tools: For readers tracking OpenAI’s ad expansion, monitor the official OpenAI Ads portal and ChatGPT Ads documentation for self-service options. Those interested in privacy protections can explore open-source ad-blocking lists like EasyList and uBlock Origin filters. For comparison, check Anthropic’s Claude product updates and Google’s AI ad offerings in Performance Max to see how competitors respond.
